question: A 33-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of worsening shortness of breath and fatigue. Her paternal uncle had similar symptoms and died of respiratory failure at 45 years of age. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Pulmonary function testing shows an FVC of 84%, an FEV1/FVC ratio of 92%, and a normal diffusion capacity. An ECG shows a QRS axis greater than +90 degrees. Genetic analysis shows an inactivating mutation in the bone morphogenetic protein receptor type II (BMPR2) gene. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Inactivating mutation in BMPR2 gene" -> "disruption of pulmonary vascular homeostasis" -> "increased pulmonary arterial pressure" -> "worsening shortness of breath and fatigue" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Genetic mutation affecting BMPR2" -> "impaired regulation of vascular smooth muscle" -> "pulmonary vasoconstriction" -> "elevated pulmonary arterial pressure" -> "symptoms of dyspnea and fatigue" -> 90%

CHAIN: "BMPR2 mutation" -> "abnormal pulmonary artery remodeling" -> "increased resistance in pulmonary circulation" -> "elevated pulmonary arterial pressure" -> "shortness of breath and fatigue" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Mutation in BMPR2" -> "pulmonary vascular disease" -> "increased pressure in pulmonary arteries" -> "symptoms of respiratory distress" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of worsening shortness of breath and fatigue, along with the family history of similar symptoms and early death, suggest a hereditary condition. The pulmonary function tests indicate a preserved FEV1/FVC ratio and normal diffusion capacity, which is consistent with a condition that does not primarily affect lung parenchyma. The inactivating mutation in the BMPR2 gene is associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), leading to elevated pulmonary arterial pressure. This is further supported by the ECG findings of a right axis deviation, which can occur in the setting of right heart strain due to elevated pressures. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms is elevated pulmonary arterial pressure.
